_doc: Story cases (StoryManager + CustomerManager): the THREAD mystery walking in through the door as ordinary patients. Each case takes a routine patient's place in the day's schedule, in order, within its acts (act .. last_act), when `when` holds (StoryManager.cond), a few days apart (time.json pacing.story_case_gap_days). patient: who they are (archetype / faction / category steer the generator; looks, chrome, budget and the job come from the street like anyone else's; id keeps them the same person across visits). line, history and clue are what they say, what the file says and what the scan finds (each may have *_variants: [{if: cond, text}]). on_arrive / on_success / on_failed / on_declined: StoryManager effects. after / after_failed: the decision (an event in events.json) that follows the operation.

cases.line: Union wants a grip servo on my left arm. Funny thing, doc: my hands haven't shaken since the free clinic van. Nerve tonic, they called it. One shot, no charge. Steady as a crane.
cases.history: Free 'nerve tonic' injection from an outreach van on the Low Line, six weeks ago. No paperwork.
cases.clue: Under the old scar: silver filaments, finer than hair, running along the nerve. Not chrome. Not in any catalogue you own.

cases.line: (Her mother does the talking.) She used to scream at me. Now it's 'yes, mama' to everything. The van gave her the tonic for her fits. Fix her eyes so she can read the price tags. And tell me why she's so quiet.
cases.history: Seizures since age nine. Seizure-free since a free 'tonic' from an outreach van, two months ago. Mother reports 'unusual calm'.
cases.clue: The same silver filaments along the optic nerve. Denser than Bram's. They branch toward the speech centres.

cases.line: There's a dial tone in my head between stations. Like someone's tuning me. Your scan's going to say I'm fine. Everybody's scan says I'm fine.

line_variants.text: There's a dial tone in my head between stations, like someone's tuning me. A crane jockey in my block said you'd find the silver in him. Find it in me.

cases.history: Paid 'sleep study' in Meridian Heights, three months ago. Tinnitus 'like a radio' since.
cases.clue: The port's handshake log: LYR-THREAD v0.9 asked for permission 3,112 times. It was granted 3,112 times. Nobody granted it.

cases.line: Mother sent me for plating. Half the crew got the free shot when the van came through the Belt. Now they stand where they're told and they don't ask why. Mother likes it. I don't.
cases.history: Declined the outreach van's shot. 'Didn't trust anything free.'
cases.clue: No filaments in him. But the knife wounds on his back were stitched by someone who knows Lyra's closing pattern.

cases.line: I file the Board's seizure reports. 'Unknown cause', every one, and every one closed by the same upstairs code before anyone reads it. I need new eyes. Mine are tired of reading them.
cases.history: Civil servant, 24 years. Paying cash 'so it doesn't show up on the Board's health plan'.
cases.clue: Eye strain, nothing more. Her badge has a records clearance you've only seen on inspectors.

cases.line: Rook says you're the one cutter who doesn't talk to Aegis. Their checkpoint put two rounds in my shoulder. Fix the arm, doc. Rook's paying, and Rook pays well.

line_variants.text: Rook says you warned us about the van when nobody else would. Aegis put two rounds in my shoulder at the Belt. Fix the arm, doc. Rook's paying, and Rook pays well.

cases.history: Gunshot wounds, left shoulder, under 24 hours old. Treated in a stairwell with tape. Referred by Rook Varga.
cases.clue: Two Aegis-issue slugs, still in the joint. Somebody will be asking who took them out.

cases.line: Aegis medical takes notes. You don't, I'm told. Someone who wasn't us rerouted my optic. I want it back to factory, quietly. Aegis pays well for quiet.
cases.history: Corporate security officer. Optic firmware altered off-network. Paying with corporate scrip, no insurance claim.
cases.clue: The optic's log has been edited by hand. Whoever did it knew Aegis codes, and knew where she'd be looking.

cases.line: Okafor says you don't take sides. Neither do we. Turns out that's rarer than chrome down here. Knee's shot. I run for a living.

line_variants.text: Okafor heard you handed an Aegis retainer back across the table. Nobody does that. Knee's shot, doc. I run for a living, and I'd rather run for people like you.
Okafor heard you patched a Rustline lieutenant and didn't sell him, or keep him. That's our kind of doctor. Knee's shot. I run for a living.

cases.history: Freelance courier. Pays in exact change. Refuses to say who for.
cases.clue: Old courier wear and nothing else. The cleanest knee you've opened this year.

cases.line: Bed 14, Meridian trial wing. I walked out in a laundry van. They put a lattice in me, doctor, and it's growing toward my voice. I want it out. I can't pay much. They'll come looking.
cases.history: Enrolled in Lyra Biocomp's 'Community Neural Wellness' trial. Wristband still on: a contact number, no name.
cases.clue: A woven lattice the width of a hand, rooted along the vagus nerve. Lyra part numbers etched into the anchors. This is THREAD, finished.

cases.line: Wire sold my log. Three buyers, and one of them came in through my port and wiped a year out of me. You were the only other one who saw that log, doc. Fix the port. Then we'll talk about it.
cases.history: Returning patient. Port wiped from the inside; memory gaps of about a year. Says he knows who sold him.
cases.clue: The port's been scrubbed by a corporate tool. The same LYR signature, signing its work this time.

cases.line: Remember me? Steady hands. Steady everything. I can't stop being steady, doc. I sit where they put me. Help me get up.

line_variants.text: You told me. I laughed. Now my hands are steady and my head's full of radio, and I sit where they put me. Get it out, doc. Please.
They say you kept a piece of me in a jar. Good. Then you know what's in here. My head's full of radio, doc. Help me get up.

cases.history: Returning patient. Left grip servo (your work). Absent from Pier 9 for three weeks: 'follows instructions, initiates nothing'.
cases.clue: The filaments have become a lattice. It has your servo's wiring wrapped in it like ivy on a fence.

cases.line: I sing at the night market now. Badly, and every night. Lyra's been asking around for my surgeon. I didn't tell them. I brought you something from Bed 14 instead.
cases.history: Returning patient. Lattice removed (your work). Voice recovering. Wants the old trial port closed for good.
cases.clue: The scar from the lattice has healed clean. The anchors you left are inert. Your work held.

cases.line: Doctor. Community Neural Wellness thanks you for your cooperation. I'm here for a routine adjustment. Please don't look at me like that. I don't remember why you would.
cases.history: Lyra Biocomp liaison. Company-paid. Records list no prior visits to this clinic.
cases.clue: The lattice is still there, finished and quiet. It has grown around the nerve that carries her voice.
